correctness.rationale: The complete proof consists of an established and directly reconstructed three-move chain cutoff, a disjoint-component Duplicator strategy, rank-three antichain sentences separating component counts, and exhaustive exact Hintikka signature calculation on all 119 capped canonical tuples. Every atomic diagram includes equality and both order directions; a second nonrecursive triple-profile realization of the same recursion agrees on all cases. The exact program was executed from its packaged source and yielded 7,27,68 classes and sharp bounds 7,13,19. Sampling past the cutoff is supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Direct sums of finite chains are a canonical poset decomposition; classifying their shallow first-order theories without naming components is a natural finite-model question. The 17 nontrivial mergers among 119 capped tuples and the sharp 19-vertex threshold express real interaction among incomparable components, beyond the familiar separate-chain cutoff. This is an exact complete natural classification for up to three components rather than an arbitrary slice or a renamed textbook consequence.
